    Ordinary arrows and one-sided generating contours #

    def:generating-rays(3), the path part of lem:generating-paths, and prop:controlled-contours (Appendix C.1 in that paper).

    An ordinary path for a ray f starts with an ordinary left divisor of f, and every ordinary left divisor starts such a path. We prove prop:controlled-contours in the form used by lem:one-sided-path-coefficients: a generating ray of type L has exactly one ordinary left divisor (all its ordinary paths start with the same arrow), and dually for type R. The proof is that of Appendix C.1 applied to two paths with distinct first (respectively last) arrows: the crown and the six-point tree fix their types, and the six-lift and eight-lift trees exclude the remaining case.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
